title: ECHO: Elastic Speculative Decoding with Sparse Gating for High-Concurrency Scenarios
claim: Verification cost grows to dominate as concurrency rises, so a state-of-the-art accelerator loses its speedup and falls below the baseline.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, line plot beside grouped bar chart
description: The figure has two side-by-side plots with a shared x-axis, batch size. The left panel, titled LLaMA3.3-70B, is a line chart of latency in ms against batch size from 1 to 256. A red dotted line with stars (T_t, verification) stays flat near 120 ms at small batch sizes, then curves sharply upward to about 1000 ms at BS=256. A blue solid line with squares (T_AR per token) stays near 100–230 ms. A green line with diamonds (T_d) sits at zero. The right panel, titled Qwen3-235B, is a grouped bar chart of throughput in tokens/s for EAGLE-3 (red) and AR (blue) at batch sizes 1 to 128. Red bars lead at small and medium batch sizes. At BS=128 the blue AR bar is taller, around 1560 against 1140. The eye goes first to the steep red curve and the reversed bars on the right.
caption: Performance degradation in high-concurrency scenarios on MT-Bench. Left: Latency breakdown for LLaMA-3.3-70B. Verification cost ($T_t$) scales linearly, becoming the dominant bottleneck over AR cost ($T_{AR}$) as batch size increases. Right: Throughput for Qwen3-235B. Due to this bottleneck, the speedup of EAGLE-3 diminishes and eventually underperforms vanilla AR at high concurrency (BS=128).
abstract: Speculative Decoding promises to accelerate the inference of Large Language Models, yet its efficacy often degrades in production-grade serving. Existing evaluations typically overlook the compute-bound nature of high-concurrency regimes, where verification compute becomes the dominant bottleneck. Consequently, prior methods face a dilemma: static trees incur massive verification waste, while dynamic trees suffer from cumulative misjudgments and kernel incompatibility. To bridge this gap, we introduce ECHO, a high concurrency-oriented framework integrated into SGLang that reformulates speculative execution as a budgeted scheduling problem. Crucially, ECHO employs sparse confidence gating to manage the batch as a unified super-tree, elastically pivoting budget between depth and width to co-optimize the trade-off between reducing global verification steps and maximizing per-step efficiency. Extensive evaluations across diverse model scales-particularly the industrial-grade Qwen3-235B-demonstrate that ECHO consistently outperforms SOTA methods in both low-load and high-load scenarios, achieving up to 5.35x walltime speedup and delivering over 20% relative speedup gain.
